skill.name: pricewin-flight-search
skill.description: Search live flight fares from Agoda, Trip.com, and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server. Compare schedules, stops, prices, and provider booking links.
skill.summary: Compare live flight fares and schedules across three travel sites.
skill.author: PriceWin

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, or disclosed configuration paths. The installer still modifies several user-level agent configurations and persistently registers a closed-source remote MCP service. Flight searches disclose route and trip details to that service.

remediation.issue: The installer registers the endpoint across every detected agent.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit client selection and confirmation before each configuration change. Default to dry-run output.

remediation.issue: The configured MCP service is closed source and can change independently.
remediation.suggestion: Publish auditable server code or provide a verifiable deployment and tool manifest. Document change control for remote tool behavior.
Write to a temporary file, validate the result, preserve permissions, and atomically replace the original after creating a protected backup.

remediation.issue: Travel query details are sent to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Show a clear consent notice before the first query and avoid sending optional free-text content.

content.user_title: Compare Live Flight Fares Across Travel Sites
content.value_statement: Flight prices vary across travel sites and can be difficult to compare consistently. This skill searches PriceWin data and presents ranked fares with booking links.
actual_capabilities: Starts one-way or return searches using IATA codes, dates, passenger counts, and cabin class.
Polls asynchronous PriceWin sessions until fares arrive or the search fails.
Compares merged fares from Agoda, Trip.com, and Traveloka.
Ranks flights by party-total price while highlighting practical nonstop or shorter options.
Presents airline, schedule, duration, stops, currency, and returned provider links.
Separates outbound and return results as independently priced one-way tickets.
limitations: Requires a configured PriceWin MCP server, whose hosted implementation is closed source.
Cannot resolve ambiguous city names or choose among multiple airports without user input.
Cannot book flights, accept payments, or guarantee that displayed fares remain available.
Search coverage can be partial while providers are unavailable, blocked, or still responding.

use_cases.title: Compare a personal trip
use_cases.description: Find affordable flights for fixed dates and compare price, duration, stops, and departure times.

use_cases.title: Prepare client options
use_cases.description: Build a concise shortlist of practical fares before a client selects a provider.

use_cases.title: Research business travel
use_cases.description: Compare nonstop and shorter schedules against the lowest fare for a planned work trip.

prompt_templates.title: Search a one-way flight
prompt_templates.prompt: Find one-way economy flights from [ORIGIN IATA] to [DESTINATION IATA] on [DATE] for [ADULTS] adults.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search with known airport codes

prompt_templates.title: Compare a return journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Search flights from [ORIGIN] to [DESTINATION] on [DEPARTURE DATE], returning [RETURN DATE]. Show the best options for each leg.

prompt_templates.title: Balance price and convenience
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare business-class flights from [ORIGIN] to [DESTINATION] on [DATE]. Prioritize nonstop options when the price difference is small.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze options for a group
prompt_templates.prompt: Search [CABIN] flights for [ADULTS] adults from [ORIGIN] to [DESTINATION] on [DATE]. Explain party totals, per-person estimates, and schedule tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Find one-way economy flights from SGN to BKK next Friday for two adults.
output: The results list the cheapest available flights first.
Each option includes airline, flight number, times, duration, stops, and the total fare for two adults.
The response includes only provider links returned by the search.

output_examples.input: Compare return flights from HAN to SIN and highlight practical nonstop choices.
output: Outbound and return options appear under separate headings.
The lowest fare is identified, with a nearby nonstop alternative highlighted when useful.
Any combined estimate is labeled as two separately booked one-way tickets.

output_examples.input: Find business-class flights from Tokyo to Seoul without choosing an airport for me.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks which Tokyo and Seoul airports to use before starting the search.

best_practices: Provide three-letter IATA codes and ask before resolving cities with multiple airports.
Read the returned currency and passenger count before describing any fare.
Recheck availability and price on the provider page before purchase.
anti_patterns: Do not invent airport codes, fares, provider names, or booking links.
Do not describe independently searched return legs as one quoted round-trip fare.
Do not send names, payment details, or unrelated conversation through free-text search fields.

faq.question: Which travel sites are compared?
faq.answer: The PriceWin service merges flight fares collected from Agoda, Trip.com, and Traveloka.

faq.question: Can this skill book a flight?
faq.answer: No. It compares fares and returns provider links where users can verify details and complete a purchase.

faq.question: Does the skill need airport codes?
faq.answer: Yes. Origin and destination must be three-letter IATA codes.

faq.question: Are prices per traveler?
faq.answer: No. The returned price is the total for all requested adults on one leg.

faq.question: Why can results change?
faq.answer: Fares are time-sensitive and can change because of provider availability, caching, inventory, or crawl progress.

faq.question: What data reaches PriceWin?
faq.answer: The service receives route codes, travel dates, passenger counts, cabin class, and the generated session identifier.
